# axiom_monitor (Resource)



## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "axiom_monitor" "threshold" {
  name             = "Error rate"
  type             = "Threshold"
  apl_query        = "['http-logs'] | where status >= 500 | summarize count() by bin_auto(_time)"
  interval_minutes = 5
  range_minutes    = 5
  operator         = "Above"
  threshold        = 100
}

# Named levels set threshold to the most severe level's value.
resource "axiom_monitor" "threshold_levels" {
  name             = "Error rate levels"
  type             = "Threshold"
  apl_query        = "['http-logs'] | where status >= 500 | summarize count() by bin_auto(_time)"
  interval_minutes = 5
  range_minutes    = 5
  operator         = "Above"
  thresholds = [
    { name = "Page on-call", severity = "critical", value = 500, recovery = 400 },
    { name = "Heads up", severity = "warning", value = 100 },
  ]
}

# On an anomaly monitor, level values are tolerances in standard deviations,
# and tolerance is set to the most severe level's value.
resource "axiom_monitor" "anomaly_levels" {
  name             = "Request volume anomaly"
  type             = "AnomalyDetection"
  apl_query        = "['http-logs'] | summarize count() by bin_auto(_time)"
  interval_minutes = 5
  range_minutes    = 60
  compare_days     = 7
  operator         = "Above"
  thresholds = [
    { name = "Page on-call", severity = "critical", value = 4 },
    { name = "Heads up", severity = "warning", value = 2, recovery = 1.5 },
  ]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Monitor name
- `type` (String) The type of the monitor. Possible values include: 'Threshold', 'AnomalyDetection', 'MatchEvent'

### Optional

- `alert_on_no_data` (Boolean) If the monitor should trigger an alert if there is no data
- `apl_query` (String) The APL query used inside the monitor (mutually exclusive with mpl_query)
- `compare_days` (Number) The number of days to compare for anomaly detection
- `delay` (Number) The delay in seconds before the monitor runs (useful for situations where data is batched/delayed)
- `description` (String) Monitor description
- `disabled_until` (String) The time the monitor will be disabled until
- `interval_minutes` (Number) How often the monitor should run
- `labels` (Set of String) Set of existing Axiom label IDs assigned to this resource. Omit to leave assignments unchanged; use an empty set to clear all assignments.
- `mpl_query` (String) The MPL query used inside the monitor (mutually exclusive with apl_query)
- `notifier_ids` (List of String) A list of notifier id's to be used when this monitor triggers
- `notify_by_group` (Boolean) If the monitor should track non-time groups separately
- `notify_every_run` (Boolean) Indicates whether to send notifications on every trigger
- `operator` (String) Operator used in monitor trigger evaluation
- `range_minutes` (Number) Query time range from now
- `resolvable` (Boolean) Determines whether the events triggered by the monitor are individually resolvable. This has no effect on threshold monitors
- `skip_resolved` (Boolean) Specifies whether to skip resolved alerts
- `threshold` (Number) The threshold where the monitor should trigger. When `thresholds` is set on a Threshold monitor, this is computed as the value of the most severe level
- `thresholds` (Attributes Set) Named threshold levels of a Threshold or AnomalyDetection monitor, from 1 to 4. Names and severities must be unique. On a Threshold monitor, values must be ordered in the operator's direction, with the most severe level furthest out. On an AnomalyDetection monitor, values are tolerances in standard deviations, greater than 0 and at most 100, that increase with severity, and the operator must be Above or Below. Removing `thresholds` removes the levels and leaves `threshold` (0 unless set) as the monitor's only value, or `tolerance` on an AnomalyDetection monitor, which must then be set. More than one level requires the threshold levels feature for the organization (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--thresholds))
- `tolerance` (Number) The tolerance for anomaly detection, in standard deviations. When `thresholds` is set on an AnomalyDetection monitor, this is computed as the value of the most severe level
- `trigger_after_n_positive_results` (Number) The number of positive results needed before triggering
- `trigger_from_n_runs` (Number) The number of consecutive check runs that must trigger before triggering an alert

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) The timestamp when the monitor was created
- `created_by` (String) The ID of the user who created the monitor
- `id` (String) Monitor identifier

<a id="nestedatt--thresholds"></a>
### Nested Schema for `thresholds`

Required:

- `name` (String) Level name
- `severity` (String) Level severity. One of `critical`, `error`, `warning` or `info`
- `value` (Number) The value where the level triggers. On an AnomalyDetection monitor, a tolerance in standard deviations

Optional:

- `recovery` (Number) The value the query result must cross for the level to resolve. Defaults to `value` and must be on the resolving side of it. On an AnomalyDetection monitor, a tolerance from 0 to `value`
